newsitem.title: UK: UK's Waldegrave hopes PSBR beats official f/cast.
newsitem.headline: UK's Waldegrave hopes PSBR beats official f/cast.

text.p: Britain is on track to meet its PSBR forecast for 1996/97 and may even beat it, Treasury Chief Secretary William Waldegrave said on Wednesday.

"This has been an excellent month for the public finances. We are now clearly on track to meet the forecast for the Public Sector Borrowing Requirement and I am hopeful that we will do better than that," he said in a speech prepared for delivery to businessmen in London.

January PSBR data on Tuesday showed a monthly repayment of 5.8 billion stg, allowing the PSBR for the fiscal year so far to drop to 10.893 billion stg with only two months to come in this fiscal year. The Treasury has forecast the PSBR will total 26.4 billion stg.

"It is Conservative policies which have given Britain stronger public finances than most other EU countries," Waldegrave said. "Labour's policies would utterly reverse our hard work. Labour would increase public spending and push up borrowing."
